name: Excise Tax by Token of Trust
author: Token of Trust

sections.description:
This plugin calculates excise taxes for WooCommerce stores selling regulated goods
such as vape, nicotine pouches and hemp products.

  • Real-time calculation – Excise taxes are calculated at checkout, for both the legacy and block-based WooCommerce checkout.
  • Product syncing – Product attributes needed for excise tax calculation are synced to the Token of Trust Excise Tax Products Dashboard.
  • Order syncing – Orders are reported to the Token of Trust Excise Tax Calculator as they are placed, paid, fulfilled and refunded, for reconciliation and reporting.
  • Wholesale and retail – Configure which WordPress roles are treated as wholesalers so orders are taxed correctly.

This plugin can run on its own, or side-by-side with the main Token of Trust plugin.
When the main Token of Trust plugin is active, it provides the tax functionality and
this plugin stays out of the way.

You need an active Token of Trust account to use this plugin.

External services

This plugin is a client for Token of Trust, a paid excise tax service. Excise
tax rates depend on product classification and on state, county and city rules
that change continually, so the calculation is performed by Token of Trust
rather than in your WordPress install. The plugin cannot calculate excise tax on
its own, and no feature of the plugin is locked behind a payment check.

Nothing is sent anywhere until you enter a Token of Trust license key or choose
to create an account in the setup wizard. On a fresh install this plugin
contacts no external service at all.

Token of Trust (tokenoftrust.com)

The plugin talks to two Token of Trust hosts: app.tokenoftrust.com for your
live account and sandbox.tokenoftrust.com for test mode. It contacts them as
follows.

  • Creating an account – if you create an account through the setup wizard,
    the plugin sends your store’s domain, your site title, the name and email
    address of the WordPress administrator completing the form, and the plugin’s
    version, and then the confirmation code emailed to that address.
  • Licensing – when your license key is saved or refreshed, the plugin sends
    the license key and your store’s domain to both hosts to confirm the account
    and retrieve the live and test API credentials used by the calls below.
  • Calculating excise tax – at cart and checkout, and again after payment,
    the plugin sends the shipping or pickup address for the order, and for each
    line item the quantity, unit price, discounted price, product ID and SKU, plus
    whether the order is wholesale or retail and an internal reference for the
    order, which can include the customer’s WordPress user ID. It receives back
    the tax amount and the label shown on the order.
  • Recording orders – order syncing is on by default, and stays on while
    Token of Trust is collecting excise tax for your account. While it is on, the
    plugin sends a record of each order as it is placed, paid, fulfilled or
    refunded: the customer’s first and last name, the shipping address, the line
    items above with shipped and refunded quantities, the tax collected, and the
    order date. This is what the Token of Trust Excise Tax Calculator reconciles
    against. You can also send the orders from a date range yourself.
  • Syncing products – when product syncing is enabled, the plugin sends the
    excise tax attributes you enter on each product, along with its name and SKU,
    and when you open a product it fetches the attributes stored for its SKUs.
  • Receiving updates – Token of Trust can call your site at
    /token-of-trust/webhooks to tell it that your account settings changed, to
    ask for the orders from a date range to be sent again (only while order
    syncing is on), or to turn on debug logging for a set number of hours. Debug
    logs are kept in your WordPress database and shown on the plugin’s Logs
    screen. These requests are rejected unless they carry a valid signature.

Token of Trust: https://tokenoftrust.com/
Terms of service: https://tokenoftrust.com/legal/end-user-terms/
Privacy policy: https://tokenoftrust.com/legal/privacy-policy/

Source code

The setup wizard is a React application. The plugin loads the compiled bundle
from Admin/SetupWizard/build/, and its full, human-readable source ships with
the plugin in the source/ directory:

  • source/tax-wizard/ – the Excise Tax setup wizard.
  • source/wizard-ui/ – shared components the wizard is built from.

To rebuild the bundle, install Node.js 16 or later, then run
npm install && npm run build inside source/tax-wizard/. The build writes
to Admin/SetupWizard/build/, replacing the shipped files.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it through the WordPress “Plugins” screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. You are taken to the Token of Trust setup screen, which is also under the “Token of Trust” menu.
  3. Create a Token of Trust account there, or enter the license key you were given.
  4. Choose your excise tax settings: the roles treated as wholesalers, and whether products and orders are synced.
sections.faq:
Do I need the main Token of Trust plugin as well?

No. This plugin is self-contained and handles excise tax calculation on its own. If the
main Token of Trust plugin is also active, it takes over the tax functionality and this
plugin defers to it, so the two can safely run side-by-side.

Does this work with the WooCommerce block checkout?

Yes. Excise tax calculation is supported for both the legacy checkout and the
block-based checkout.

Where do I get support?

Contact us at https://tokenoftrust.com/contact/ or
email support@tokenoftrust.com.
sections.changelog:
1.1.2

  • Internal data names now carry a longer prefix, as the WordPress.org plugin directory requires. Your settings, licence and queued order syncs are carried over automatically on update; nothing needs to be re-entered.
  • The setup screen no longer waits indefinitely when your licence cannot be confirmed. It now says the licence is not working and offers to check again.
  • The account step is no longer ticked while the licence is being refused, so the checklist shows what is actually set up.
  • A store keeps working from its last confirmed licence when Token of Trust cannot be reached, instead of behaving as though no licence was entered.

1.1.1

  • The excise tax settings page has a new address. Old links redirect to it, so bookmarks keep working.
  • The role selectors on that page now use WooCommerce’s own enhanced dropdown, so the plugin no longer carries its own copy of one.

1.1.0

  • Added Nicotine Pouch and Hemp product types to excise tax product sync.
  • Product fields now change to match the selected product type.
  • Renamed “Exempt from Vape Taxes” to “Exempt from Excise Taxes”; it now applies to all product types.
  • Admin scripts and styles are now versioned, so an upgrade no longer serves stale cached assets.

1.0.0

  • Initial release of the standalone excise tax plugin, which can operate side-by-side with the main Token of Trust plugin.
